material.notes: AUDIT 15 (matched to review): own comparer (template placement, flat px off beyond 2 px of the reference ink). Every chip variant is exact except the input chip: its remove icon is not the reference shape (18 to 26 flat px off, 12 to 14 ring px, in rest, hover, focus, pressed and disabled, both schemes), and the selected input chip is far off in light (148 px at rest, 71 to 79 in hover, focus and pressed). | Compared with Material Web (docs/ui/looks/ref/material) at 100 % on the strict metric (a reference structural pixel is off when ours differs by more than 2 levels; text and icon ink within 2 px excluded, glyph-counted separately; every pixel outside the control's box compared, so shadows and state layers count): 45 states compared, 0 over the line (off + outside + ring above 0.3 % of the structural pixels, 40 at least); worst state 40 px, worst glyph-only count 24 px.
gaps: Input chip: the remove icon is the Symbols close the capture draws, 1 px off in x because the sheet centres a chip on a whole pixel but its width is fractional (the 18 to 26 px of each input chip cell)
The capture of a focused input chip no longer forces the state layer of its remove button (the focus stands on the chip), and a chip carries enabled, elevated and leading icon forms

Evidence: Material Web 1.x rendered in Chromium with greyscale text and unhinted glyphs (round 26; the earlier captures carried ClearType fringes; round 28 re-captured the corrected cells), focus is the 10 % state layer, pressed 10 %, M3 tracking set to zero as Neper's text engine has no letter spacing; Neper's greyscale text equals that unhinted text to within 2 levels in every text pixel of the dialog and tab cells, so no subpixel mode was added to the text engine; no Android device capture
